questions.title: Form
questions.question: Does recent form predict results once you know how good a team is?
questions.answer: No evidence. A team in better form by one standard deviation (0.98 points per game over the last five) gains +0.03 expected points per match beyond its strength. Over a season that is between -1.5 and +3.4 points.
questions.detail: Strength models already capture most of what a run of results tells you. Windows of 3 and 10 matches, and form in all competitions, tell the same story.

questions.title: Rest
questions.question: Does having more rest than the opponent help?
questions.answer: No evidence. One standard deviation more rest (1.8 days) is worth +0.00 expected points per match.
questions.detail: Tested on 2022/23 to 2024/25, the test seasons where every cup and European fixture is in the open data.

questions.title: Midweek Europe
questions.question: Does a European match in the previous five days hurt?
questions.answer: No evidence. The estimate points the expected way (-0.03 points per match per standard deviation) but is well within the noise.
questions.detail: Clubs in Europe are strong and rotate squads; once strength is accounted for, the midweek game leaves no detectable mark.

questions.title: Travel
questions.question: Do longer away trips help the home side?
questions.answer: No evidence after correction. Each extra 110 km of travel for the away side is worth +0.06 points per match to the home side (unadjusted p = 0.05, 0.32 after correction).
questions.detail: This was the closest call. With the closing market as the control the estimate shrinks and is not significant even before correction.

questions.title: Weather and goals
questions.question: Do temperature, rain or wind change the number of goals?
questions.answer: No evidence. The largest weather effect is -0.01 goals per match per standard deviation, against an average of 2.95 goals.
questions.detail: Weather is ERA5 reanalysis at each ground for the hour of kick-off.

questions.title: Weather and who wins
questions.question: Does rain or wind level the field between favourite and underdog?
questions.answer: No evidence after correction. Heavier rain moved -0.08 expected points per match away from the favourite per standard deviation (unadjusted p = 0.05, 0.32 after correction).
questions.detail: A result worth retesting on future seasons, not a finding.

questions.title: Money
questions.question: Does wage spending explain most of the variation in league points?
questions.answer: Not run yet. There is no openly licensed wage data; the test runs as soon as figures from club accounts are compiled.
questions.detail: The pre-registered test: league points on log wage bill relative to the league average, needing R-squared of at least 0.5.
questions.reason: data/manual/wages.csv has no verified club-season wage bills (OQ-04)

questions.title: Home advantage
questions.question: Is there still a home advantage?
questions.answer: Yes, a real effect. Home sides outscore away sides by 0.31 goals per match (0.25 to 0.37) in matches with crowds.
questions.detail: Because every pair of teams meets home and away, the average home goal difference is free of team strength.

questions.title: Is home advantage fading?
questions.question: Has home advantage declined since 2014/15?
questions.answer: No evidence. The trend is -0.11 goals per decade (-0.26 to +0.05): consistent with a modest decline, and with none.
questions.detail: 2024/25 was the lowest season in the sample, but one low season is not a trend.

side_finding.title: Empty stadiums
side_finding.label: Side finding
side_finding.answer: Without crowds, home sides scored 1.06 times their away rate, against 1.19 with crowds. The point estimate says about 64% of the home goal advantage went with the fans, but the interval includes no change.

exploratory.title: New manager bounce
exploratory.text: Teams took 0.64 points per game in the five matches before a sacking and 1.19 after. Against the strength model the five after were +0.04 points per match, not a real change: the bounce is mostly a bad run ending.

exploratory.title: Kick-off time
exploratory.text: Evening kick-offs showed +0.10 home points per match against afternoon games (joint test p = 0.10). Exploratory and uncorrected.

exploratory.title: Referees
exploratory.text: No evidence that referees differ in home results (joint p = 0.82, 28 referees).

exploratory.title: After international breaks
exploratory.text: No evidence of a home or favourite effect in the first round after a break (541 matches).
